questions.question: Describe the main health risks for miners.
questions.expected_answer: Breathing silica dust over many years can cause silicosis, which scars the lungs, cannot be cured and makes TB more likely; coal dust can also cause lung disease. Loud noise can cause permanent hearing loss. Heat can cause heat exhaustion and heatstroke, and heavy work in low stopes can injure backs, knees and joints. Stress and long periods away from home affect mental health and families.

questions.question: Describe the main safety risks in mines.
questions.expected_answer: Underground risks include rock falls and rockbursts, accidents with machines, trains and conveyor belts, falls, explosions from explosives or methane and coal dust, fires that fill tunnels with smoke, flooding, and dangerous gases or lack of oxygen. In surface mines, risks include accidents with giant trucks, rock falling from pit walls, and blasting.

questions.question: How are miners protected by rules, equipment and rights?
questions.expected_answer: The Mine Health and Safety Act of 1996 sets the rules, and inspectors check that mines follow them. Mines must provide protective equipment, self-rescuers, refuge bays, rock support, ventilation, dust and noise control, training, check-ups and rescue teams. Miners have the right to be trained, to elect safety representatives, and to leave a dangerous place, and a duty to wear equipment and follow rules. Sick or injured miners can get compensation.
